goal: Roadmap R40: when a change breaks an artifact the kit generated in other repos (a phase spec, a verify-<app> skill, a REVIEW.md), the PR lists the watched repos that hold one and names the upgrade PR for each.
changed: `quality.py sweep BOOKS_DIR KIND` lists the watched repos whose default branch holds the artifact, read from GitHub's file list and not from a checkout. `--at DAY` reads the branch as it was that day.
The list names public repos only. A repo the books do not count as public is not asked about and not named, only counted, unless `--with-private` is given.
The Authoring a skill playbook has the rule as step 7, and agent-kit's checklist has a `format-sweep` item that asks for the list when a diff touches those formats.

The replay against the 0.12.0 spec change lists no repo: none of the three public watched repos held a phase spec that day. The roadmap's done-when expected a list of product repos, and the public list is empty.

claims.claim: Replayed against the 0.12.0 spec change (`sweep phase-spec --at 2026-11-16`, the day before commit 088cd28 landed), the public list is empty: none of the three public watched repos held a file under docs/phases/.
claims.check: quality.py sweep on the quality books against the real GitHub API, macOS, Python 3.12
claims.remaining: The run used today's watch list, not the list of 2026-11-16. The private watched repo is not in this output by design: its answer was read with --with-private and is kept out of this repo.

claims.claim: sweep finds real artifacts: today it lists the two public repos that hold a verify skill and the one that holds a REVIEW.md, and works where `gh auth status` fails.
claims.check: quality.py sweep verify-skill and review-guide on the quality books against the real GitHub API. The auth probe ran sweep behind a gh whose `auth status` exits 1: same output, exit 0, three `gh api` calls.
claims.remaining: `git ls-tree` on each public repo's local origin/main gave the same answer in all twelve cells. No real repo's file list was large enough for GitHub to cut it short: that path is covered by a test on a made-up answer.

claims.claim: By default a private watched repo is never asked about and nothing of it is printed, on success, with --json, with --at, and when every call fails. A repo with no visibility row, a failed lookup or a private row in its past counts as private.
claims.check: tests/test_quality_sweep.py, PrivateRepoTest, on made-up books with one private repo and a fake gh that logs every call. With the filter removed, or with a second privacy rule in place of private_repos, these tests fail.
claims.remaining: A fixture. On the real books the default output was read by hand and passed leak-check.

claims.claim: The `format-sweep` checklist item fires on the commit that made the 0.12.0 spec change and stays quiet on a docs-only commit.
claims.remaining: Its paths have no pattern, so any edit to the six format files asks the question, breaking or not.

claims.claim: An agent that follows step 7 of the Authoring a skill playbook runs the sweep and puts the list and the upgrade PRs in its PR.
claims.remaining: No eval ran on the new playbook text, and no breaking format change has shipped since.

next.item: Decide whether a product repo must be on the watch list before the kit generates artifacts in it
next.why_now: The sweep reads only `watched.csv`, and the watch list changes over time. A repo that holds a phase spec and is not watched never appears in any sweep.
next.impact: Left alone, the next breaking format change can still miss a repo, and the PR's list will look complete.

next.item: R29: read the checklist from the base ref as well as the working tree
next.why_now: `format-sweep` is one more item a PR can delete or loosen in the diff it judges.
next.impact: A change that breaks a format and edits the item out gets no question.

next.item: Test step 7 on a fresh agent with a fixture change
next.why_now: The rule is prose until an agent is seen following it, and the next breaking change is the first real use.
next.impact: If agents skip the step, product repos break as they did at 0.12.0 and the script goes unused.
